name: glide-select

frames.best_why: The menu is fully open with the highlight mid-list, the tick on the current row and every option readable.

tagline: A small sort chip opens a menu whose highlight glides between rows.
summary: A compact dropdown for choosing a sort order: the chosen value sits in a dark chip, and its menu opens below with a highlight that slides from option to option. A tick marks the current choice.
appearance: The grey words Sort issues by sit before a small dark rounded chip holding Last updated and a tiny down chevron. The open menu is a slightly rounded dark panel of five rows, each with a faint letter tag at the right and a tick on the active row.
behaviour: Clicking the chip pops the menu out below and flips its chevron up. Moving across or arrowing through rows slides a lighter bar between them; picking a row closes the panel and swaps the chip label with a short blur.
demo_content: Sort issues by Last updated; options are Last updated, Newest first, Priority, Most discussed and Assignee.
use_when: A tight toolbar or filter row needs a sort or mode picker without a full-size select.
avoid_when: It is built for dark surfaces, and the small rows only suit short option labels.
customise: Pass options as strings or value, label and tag objects, plus an aria label. Size, radius, menu width, placement, align, colours, durations and disabled are props.
weight_why: A short list of rows and one sliding span, with nothing running while it is closed.

a11y.note: Full keyboard support with combobox and listbox roles, but the chip and rows show no visible focus ring.

issues: The letter tags at the right of each row are very faint.
The chip and rows have no visible focus ring, so keyboard position is unclear.
polish_why: Crisp, well-proportioned menu with a satisfying glide; dim tags and no focus ring are small misses.
